passage: Every Sunday after breakfast, Ganga knelt by the bean pot on the balcony with a plastic ruler and a pencil. She measured from the soil to the tip and wrote in her notebook, along with the weather: 6 Jul, 9 cm, dry. 13 Jul, 12 cm, cloudy. 20 Jul, 19 cm, rain on Thursday. "That's a big jump," said her neighbour Alka, peeping through the railing. Ganga turned back a page. "It rained the week before too." She underlined both rainy weeks in blue. The pattern sat there on the page, plain as anything.

qa.q: When did Ganga measure the bean plant?
qa.a: She measured it every Sunday after breakfast.

qa.q: What was Ganga feeling when she saw the pattern on the page?
qa.a: Pleased and curious, since her notes showed something she could not have seen by looking.

qa.q: What else could Ganga record to be more sure of the pattern, and why?
qa.a: She could note how much water and sunshine the plant gets, so rain can be told apart from other changes.

qa.q: How might Alka see Ganga's notebook?
qa.a: Alka is probably impressed, since Alka noticed the big jump and watched Ganga check back through the pages.

grounding: A girl measures a bean plant every Sunday, records the height, and notices it grows fastest after rain.
